tmay_2min.text: Thank you for making time to speak with me today, Maria. I appreciate it.
My name is Omar Haddad, and I'm an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028.
Before starting the program, I spent 2021 to 2026 as an analyst at Greenfield Energy Partners.
My core responsibility there was modeling solar project returns.
Over those years, that work taught me to think carefully about the assumptions that drive a project's economics,
and to appreciate how much rigor goes into deciding whether a renewable project makes financial sense.
That experience drew me further toward renewable energy finance.
My career goal is to work in renewable project finance,
and the roles I'm targeting are renewable energy project finance roles.
I'm approaching that goal with a clear sense of purpose.
I want to take the analytical foundation I built as an analyst and apply it more broadly,
moving from modeling returns on individual projects toward the larger decisions about how those projects get financed.
I see the MBA as the bridge between where I've been and where I want to go,
and I'm using this time to deepen my understanding of the field and to learn from people who have built careers in it.
That's a big reason I wanted to speak with you.
I'm especially interested in hearing how you got into renewable energy finance,
because understanding the paths others have taken helps me think more concretely about my own.
I'd also value your perspective on what it takes to grow into a role like Managing Director at Solaris Capital,
and any advice you have for someone moving from an analyst background into project finance.
